title: MB0-06156
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, his spouse, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their son, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, who are citizens of Mexico, are claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).
The father was appointed as his son's designated representative.
The claimant and his family received death threats for refusing to pay sums of money to a gang in XXXX that extorts money from people in exchange for protection.

In XXXX 2009, the gang, called "La Linea," demanded that the claimant's mother pay them a thousand dollars not to hurt her. The stress was so great that the claimant's mother had a nervous breakdown. The stress she experienced affected her health to the point that she died. The claimant, who was in the United States at the time, returned to Mexico to bury his mother.

On XXXX XXXX, 2010, he returned to the United States to save his life and the lives of his family. The gang had threatened the claimant when he was with his family. At the time of the threats, the claimant called the police. However, the police did not show much interest because corruption was rampant. The criminals reported knew that a complaint had been filed.
In addition to "La Linea," which controls XXXX, the south is controlled by the Gonzalez brothers. ANALYSIS Identity
Exhibit A-2, which includes photocopies of the claimants' original passports, identifies the claimants to the panel's satisfaction. Credibility

The claimant gave direct testimony without any contradictions. He clearly described the dangerous situation that was created by armed gangs in his country of origin, particularly in the region cited by the claimant. However, his testimony does not entitle him to be recognized as a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection." The claimant's mother, who first had problems with the demand for a ransom payment, was not able to cope. The claimant, who refused to pay the extortion money, risks being in danger because he failed to pay. If he pays the amount demanded, he will also risk being in danger because, at a certain point, the amount to be paid will be so high that he will not be able to meet it.

The prevailing situation is one of generalized violence, particularly in the claimants' region. Anyone who refuses to pay risks having problems with the drug traffickers or kidnappers who engage in extortion.

The situation the claimants face is one that is faced by many Mexicans in general, and particularly if they live in a region with highly organized drug trafficking gangs that make a lot of money and that are affiliated to other gangs.

Although the government attempts to protect its citizens, it is not able to protect the entire population. The violence that the claimant is facing is widespread and, given all the evidence and the objective situation that prevails in the claimant's region, the panel proposed an internal flight alternative in Campeche or Mexico City.

Given this reasonable alternative of being able to live in Campeche, where "La Linea" does not have a strong foothold, the claimant could live without having problems with "La Linea," which, according to the documentary evidence, seems to be absent from the Campeche region.

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, his spouse, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their son, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection."
